newsitem.title: USA: Alabama court slashes $2 million award in paint case.
newsitem.headline: Alabama court slashes $2 million award in paint case.

text.p: The Alabama Supreme Court Friday slashed a $2 million judgment against German automaker BMW in paint job liability case to $50,000 and told the plaintiff he could accept the award or opt for a new trial, his lawyer said.

The court gave Dr. Ira Gore, a Birmingham cancer specialist, 21 days to decide whether to take the judgment or choose a reversal of the original verdict and a new trial, Birmingham attorney A.W. Bolt said.
The case became a lightning rod for criticism of big jury awards when an Alabama trial court initially rendered a judgment of $4 million in punitive damages against Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG.
Gore claimed in his lawsuit that the company had sold him a $40,000 BMW with retouched paint while claiming it was a new car.

The Alabama Supreme Court reduced the $4 million award to $2 million. The U.S. Supreme Court said $2 million was too much and sent the case back to the state high court, with new guidelines, for further review.

Under the ruling issued Friday, Gore has been given a choice of accepting $50,000 in damages or having the trial court's verdict, in which BMW was found guilty of fraud, reversed. If he decides to accept the reduction, Bolt said, BMW could pay the judgment or appeal.
"He was disappointed," Bolt said of Gore when he was told of the Alabama Supreme Court decision. "Dr. Gore got cheated."

"The decision is not good for the masses," Bolt said. "Court decisions that do not require corporations to live up to an ethical standard of behavior ... send a bad message. It does not encourage good behavior."
Lawyers for BMW were not immediately available for comment.
